A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same TS-GNN research. All 42 pages of v3 and 50 pages of v4, including appendices, equations, tables and figures, support comparison. Relocated and renumbered material can be matched.

before.justification: v3 reports original node-classification experiments, including zero-shot comparisons in Table 1 and training-data scaling results in Figure 3 and Appendix D.1.

after.justification: v4 retains these original experiments and adds pretraining sensitivity, component ablations, symmetry comparisons and additional backbone results in Appendix G.

M1.justification: Section 5 generalizes the explicit feature/label sum aggregations in v3 to a permutation-invariant operator ν, allowing alternatives such as mean, max or attention. The neighborhood aggregation, least-squares mixers, adaptive biases and output projection remain. Renaming TSNet as TSNetLI does not introduce another method.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same collection of 29 node-classification datasets. The added experiments change training/test assignments, controls and backbone configurations within this collection; they introduce no new dataset, domain or task. Neither version evaluates node regression.

E2.justification: The original MeanGNN, GAT and GraphAny comparisons remain. Appendix G adds a substantial set of targeted comparisons: random prediction and non-parametric least-squares variants in Table 3, plus DSS-Mean and a zero-shot MeanGNN comparator in Table 5. MeanGNN previously appeared as an end-to-end baseline.

E3.justification: Appendix G adds four alternative single-graph training choices evaluated on 25 held-out graphs, non-parametric and component controls, padding/truncation for cross-dataset symmetry comparisons, and three additional backbone configurations. The original Table 1 and scaling protocols remain documented. The new 50% masking statement is not reconciled with retained visible-label hyperparameter ranges, so changes to the original runs are not established.

E4.justification: v3 provides transfer and training-data scaling experiments but no corresponding component or symmetry ablations. Sections G.1–G.3 add pretraining-source sensitivity, tests isolating least-squares mixing and bias, and comparisons testing feature and label symmetries. These substantially expand the evidence examining why the framework works.

E5.justification: Both versions report means and standard deviations over five random seeds. The added results follow the existing reporting practice; no changed run counts, confidence intervals or significance-testing procedures are documented.

E6.justification: Table 1, Figure 3 and the original scaling scores are unchanged, but Tables 2–6 add substantial results. Table 4 reports TS-Mean accuracies of 55.43, 63.21 and 66.21 for plain, LS and LS+bias configurations; Table 6 reports averages of 64.70, 64.34 and 62.01 for TS-SGC, TS-GCN and TS-GCNII. Table 4's full-model scores differ from retained Table 1 scores without an explained setting difference, so they do not establish version-to-version performance gains.

T1.justification: v4 adds a Schur-lemma proof of Proposition 4.1 in Appendix B, supporting representation definitions, and complexity analysis in Appendix F. It also corrects Proposition 4.1's feature-output cross-term from X^(6) to Y^(6). The appendix restatement introduces F≠C, absent from the main statement. The universality theorem and equivariant lemma already existed in v3 as Theorem 4.2 and Lemma B.28; their relocation is not new theory.

C1.justification: v4 removes the explicit claim in the introduction and Section 5 that the transformation preserves the original GNN's expressive power. It describes the recipe through general aggregation schemes more carefully. The central triple-symmetry, universality, zero-shot transfer and training-data scaling contributions remain.

C2.justification: Appendices F and G add interpretations concerning limited sensitivity to pretraining source, possible overfitting by more complex backbones in single-graph training, and memory bottlenecks from channel expansion. The earlier explanations of mixing and adaptive bias, scaling interpretation, and lack-of-regression-benchmarks limitation largely remain.

D1.justification: v4 adds a description of random label masking at each epoch and explicitly describes least-squares preprocessing as once per graph. Its 50% masking statement is not reconciled with the retained visible-label ranges. Hardware, code-access information and the existing hyperparameter tables are otherwise retained.

R1.justification: v4 adds Hamilton et al. for GraphSAGE and Wu et al. for SGC, and replaces the Pinkus citation for the universal approximation theorem with Leshno et al. The positioning against GraphAny and the discussion of the flaw in Maron et al.'s proof were already present.

P1.justification: The introduction, background and Sections 4–5 undergo substantial rewriting and notation changes. v4 distinguishes TSNetEq from TSNetLI in the main text, moves the proof strategy into Appendix D, and reorganizes the appendices into separate proof, notation, complexity, experiment, limitation and hyperparameter sections.

P2.justification: v4 adds five experimental tables, substantially expanding the tabular presentation. The six earlier tables remain as Table 1 and Tables 7–11, with Table 1 resized and the scaling table's duplicated training-count header corrected. The four figures are retained, with relocation and reference-label updates rather than new graphical findings.

improvement.justification: The added ablations and sensitivity checks improve support for the architectural choices, while removing the expressivity-preservation claim makes the scope more careful. These gains are limited by unreconciled full-model scores in Tables 1 and 4, inconsistent masking documentation, and the appendix-only F≠C assumption in the added proof. The revision improves assessability, but these inconsistencies prevent a substantial overall quality gain.
